Check out the launch trailer for Derelikt, a retro sci-fi horror first-person shooter developed by Visuwyg. The launch trailer showcases action-packed gameplay and terrifying enemies you'll face in this PS1-inspired sci-fi game.

Derelikt is available now on PlayStation 5 (PS5), Xbox Series X|S, and PC (Steam).

description:
Check out the latest trailer for Stranger Than Heaven for the upcoming action game. In the new trailer, meet protagonist Makoto Daito and learn about this character's life, whose story unfolds across five eras and five cities from 1915 to 1965.

In Act 2: Kure, Makoto Daito joins the Iwaki family following an attack on its patriarch, Genzo Iwaki, and begins his rise through the yakuza ranks. As he becomes known as the “Red Oni,” we also see Daito wrestle with his life in the yakuza and confront the choices he has made.

Stranger Than Heaven will be available on Xbox Series X/S, Xbox on PC, Xbox Clou, Xbox Game Pass, Steam, and PlayStation 5 (PS5) on January 15, 2027.

author: IGN
description: Welcome back to Next-Gen Console Watch! This week, Daemon, Ryan, and Nick take a look at Rockstar's somewhat surprising announcement that GTA 6 will be targeting 30 frames per second on all consoles—including the PS5 Pro. Many gamers, especially those who shelled out the extra bucks for the premium console, were more than a little annoyed that there won't be a 60fps or even 40fps performance mode on the Pro model. Considering the limitations of the Xbox Series X and the PS5 family, is this still acceptable in 2026? Should Rockstar have cut more corners to get 60 frames on the PS5 Pro? Plus we have some choice words from former Tekken boss Katsuhiro Harada about the Xbox Series S, and is Nintendo back in the graphics race following the success of the Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake?
title: GTA 6 Is 30fps, but We Still Have Questions - Next-Gen Console Watch

author: IGN
description:
Tanuki: Pon's Summer reviewed by Nicole Carpenter, played on PC (also available on PS4, PS5, Xbox One, Xbox Series X|S, Nintendo Switch 1 and 2).

"Tanuki: Pon's Summer launched just when it was needed most – as we head into the coldest months of the year. But it's a welcome reminder of joyful childhood summers during any time of the year, ones that were full of possibility and delight. Think of it as extreme sports delivery broken up with long stretches of roads to cruise down and minigame tasks, most of which are interesting diversions from Pon's mailman duties. Some of these minigames are monotonous and uninteresting, but they're over quick enough that it doesn't impact the game's pace too much. Over 10 hours of playtime, Tanuki: Pon's Summer is warm in both its environment and storytelling, packaged alongside simple, exciting BMX riding. Aside from a handful of lulls, though, the majority of Pon's busy vacation oozes with the warm thrill of summer that I'm finding myself daydreami
title: Tanuki: Pon's Summer Review
